atoms.b: I love my poodle. She doesn’t shed, so I have to give her a bath every two weeks. ((First --In conclusion --Soon)), I fill the bath up with some warm water. ((Next --Otherwise --Soon)), I give her a treat and rinse her body. I ((also --however --for example)) have special dog shampoo to lather her up with.

She is not the biggest fan of baths, but I think she knows they’re necessary. ((During --After --Soon)) her bath, she stays quite calm. ((However --Moreover --Today)), once the bath is over, she goes wild and runs all around the flat. ((Although --On_the_other_hand --Another)) she is small, she manages to get the whole flat wet!

instruction.text: Alma is writing in her diary after a long day. Select the transition words that she uses.

hint.text: Remember, transition words introduce new information, contrasting ideas and sometimes also show a relation in time.

atoms.b:
Dear Diary,
((Today)) I didn’t have much time to myself. ((First,)) I dropped my nephew off at school. ((Even though)) I got to my bus stop early, I ended up being late to work because the bus came 10 minutes late. ((Once)) I got to work, my colleague wouldn’t stop distracting me. ((For instance,)) he came to my desk 3 times to tell me about the features of his new microwave.

atoms.b: ((Finally,)) I told my colleague that he was preventing me from getting my work done. ((However,)) an hour later, he came back to tell me a long story about his childhood trip to Disneyland. ((In fact,)) he had already told me this story 3 times. ((At least during)) my lunch break I had some peace and quiet. ((With this in mind,)) I think I’ll start using part of my lunch break to meditate.
